name: Lab Automation and the Lab in the Loop
blurb: Robotics and closed loop labs that feed AI models.
title: Lab Automation and the Lab in the Loop
answer: AI discovery depends on fast, consistent experimental data, so automation is the other half of the loop: robots run assays, results retrain the models, and the models choose the next experiments. Liquid handling and workcell vendors are consolidating, and studies of automated labs report large cuts in manual handling.

reading.body:
Automation is the other half of the AI discovery loop: robots run assays, results retrain the models, and the models choose the next experiments.

The loop only closes if the data is consistent. A study of total laboratory automation reported an 86 percent reduction in discrete specimen handling steps and an 82 percent cut in hands-on time for add-on testing. Those are large cuts in manual handling, and they matter because a model trained on noisy, inconsistent assay output learns the noise. The section's own guidance follows from this: standardise assays and data capture before buying robots, because automation multiplies whatever data quality already exists.

Consolidation is the commercial signal. Hamilton acquired UK Robotics and Trisonic Discovery, adding a lab orchestration platform to its liquid handling range. When a liquid handling vendor buys orchestration, the bet is that the value sits in coordinating many instruments rather than in any single one. That is the same shift seen elsewhere in compute: the scarce input is not the individual machine but the system that keeps it fed.

What this does not cover is scale. There is no count of installed automated labs, no throughput figure, no cost per assay, and no named model that has been retrained by an automated loop. The evidence here is one efficiency study and one acquisition, so the claim that automation feeds AI models is stated as the premise of the field rather than demonstrated by the numbers on this page.

explainer:
Lab automation uses robots and software to run experiments: liquid handlers pipette samples, plate readers measure results, robotic arms move plates between instruments, and scheduling software orchestrates the whole workflow. Automated labs run around the clock with consistent technique, which produces the large, clean datasets AI models need.

The combination is often called the lab in the loop. A model proposes molecules or experiments, the automated lab tests them, the results flow back to retrain the model, and the next round is chosen. Each cycle improves the model where it matters for the project. The bottlenecks are rarely the robots: they are assay standardisation, data capture in consistent formats, and integration between instruments, software and models. Companies that fix those first get far more from both automation and AI.
